title: Strategic plan kickoff and sidewalk snow clearing
subtitle: Parkade agreement extension, SCADA upgrade, committee appointments, resident survey results and budget delegations on snow clearing.
overview: Council began work on its 2023-2026 Strategic Plan. It received the results of a resident satisfaction survey {{vote:m4}}, then held a first workshop at which each member shared the main themes heard from constituents during the campaign {{vote:m6}}. Common themes were affordable housing, traffic calming and road safety, climate action, and community connectedness.

Council also approved several operational items. It extended the regional Parkade agreement to June 30, 2023 {{vote:m1}}, directed staff to proceed with modernizing the sewer system's SCADA monitoring, subject to budget approval {{vote:m2}}, and approved the 2023 community appointments to boards and committees, along with updated terms of reference for the Fence Variance Committee and Committee of Adjustment {{vote:m3}}.

Four resident delegations spoke on the 2023 budget summary about sidewalk snow clearing, and council received the summary {{vote:m5}}. Residents asked for city-wide or expanded clearing, including for accessibility. Staff said more information will come with budget discussions on February 13, with options reported back for the next budget cycle. No snow clearing change was decided at this meeting.

decisions.detail: Council extended the Parkade agreement with the Region of Waterloo from January 31 to June 30, 2023, and authorized an amending agreement.
Council directed staff to start implementing the SCADA modernization, subject to 2023 budget approval, and to post the final consultant report and send the staff report to the Province.
Council approved the recommended community appointments to local boards and committees and the Fence Variance Committee and revised Committee of Adjustment terms of reference.
Council received the workshop report and each member shared three main themes heard from constituents to help shape the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan.
Council received the resident satisfaction survey results as information for strategic planning.
Council received the summary of the January 10 budget information meeting, after hearing delegations on sidewalk snow clearing.

Council enacted the by-law appointing community representatives to the Appeals Tribunal, Audit Committee, Committee of Adjustment, Fence Variance Committee and Library Board through November 14, 2026.
Council enacted the by-law appointing community representatives to various committees for the term ending November 14, 2024.

debate: Delegates argued that uncleared sidewalks and snowplow-created banks at corners block walking, transit access and accessibility, and asked for city clearing of key routes such as those near schools, transit stops and the uptown core. One delegate said the by-law complaint process is too slow and hard to use.

Delegates suggested funding ideas such as federal programs and a ward-based levy. Staff said grant funding usually covers capital rather than operating costs, and the federal program may be aimed at the Region.

Councillors raised equity and cost questions, noting that extra clearing could burden residents who are asset-rich but cash-poor. They also noted that other cities' clearing thresholds still leave many sidewalks uncleared in smaller snowfalls, and that transit stops are a regional responsibility.

Staff said about half of the roughly 170 km the city clears is sidewalk, with an earlier estimate of about three million dollars for priority routes. Options will come back through the budget discussions.

In the planning discussion, councillors said many constituents opposed 30 km/h limits outside school zones. Others raised green building standards and engaging youth, students and seniors through local groups.
